stories.title: Loveland families, businesses and staff raise $100,000 to build students an outdoor classroom
stories.summary: The Loveland Schools Foundation raised $100,000 in about six months from local businesses, families and district staff to turn a muddy picnic area into an outdoor classroom for more than 1,200 fifth- through eighth-graders.
stories.extended_summary: Starting in January 2026, the Loveland Schools Foundation set out to fix a campus space that had picnic tables but was often too muddy to use because of drainage problems. Donations from local businesses, families and district staff reached the $100,000 goal within about six months, and construction began in June. Before the 2026-27 school year, crews repaired a collapsed drain and added concrete, shade, tables and chairs at the Lebanon Road campus, which serves more than 1,200 students at Loveland Intermediate and Middle School. Principal Dr. Amanda Robinson said the space "just becomes an extension of the classroom," and Foundation board member Lynn Mangan called it "a community gathering space after school." Money raised beyond the project cost will go toward upkeep and future improvements.
stories.author: Katie Amrhein

stories.title: Empty Bowls lunch raises more than $21,000 for Loveland's LIFE Food Pantry
stories.summary: Hundreds of volunteers, local potters, restaurants and Loveland High School students came together for the fifth annual Empty Bowls fundraiser, which raised more than $21,000 for the LIFE (Loveland InterFaith Effort) Food Pantry.
stories.extended_summary: The fifth annual Empty Bowls fundraiser for LIFE Food Pantry filled Prince of Peace Lutheran Church on September 25, 2026, across two lunch seatings. Local artists donated handmade pottery bowls that every guest took home, local restaurants donated the soup, sandwiches and desserts, and local businesses donated raffle prizes. Loveland High School String Orchestra students played during lunch, and local football players stayed to clean up and reset the room. LIFE Executive Director Carol Rountree reported the event raised more than $21,000, making it the pantry's biggest fundraiser of the year. LIFE has served Loveland since 1988, providing food to hundreds of local families, stocking snack shelves in area schools and offering emergency help to families in crisis. Volunteer Brian Terry said the event "highlights the generosity and power of the Loveland community."
stories.author: Jana Hambley
